_about: Known limitations of the Trent model and report, stated so a reviewer does not have to find them. Each says whether it moves the valuation and what would fix it.

limitations.issue: Trent does not disclose revenue by format. The model works on blended sales per square foot for the whole fashion portfolio, so a faster shift of area toward Zudio and Tier II/III towns cannot be separated from like-for-like weakness; the tier-level sales per square foot (INR 15,318 / 13,390 / 12,504, AR p.119) is the only split available.
limitations.fix: A Westside/Zudio revenue split, if the company discloses one, or a format build calibrated on the tier figures and store sizes.

limitations.issue: Sales per square foot falls 5% in FY27 and 2% in FY28 and recovers from FY29. Only the FY26 decline (-14% on average area) is evidenced; like-for-like growth is disclosed only as 'low single digits' and no new-store maturity curve is disclosed. This is the largest single driver of value after margin.
limitations.fix: FY27 annual report disclosures of like-for-like growth and sales per square foot by tier; quarterly area and revenue to track the path.

limitations.issue: New area trades for 35% of its first year, calibrated on the quarterly timing of FY26 openings (Zudio 1/40/48/109 net adds). A different opening pattern in FY27 changes FY27 revenue without changing the long-run view.
limitations.fix: Quarter-by-quarter area additions, now reported in each business update.

limitations.issue: EBITDA is after Ind AS 116. Existing lease liabilities (INR 2,061 Cr) are deducted from enterprise value and new leases are charged as capex when signed (right-of-use additions, calibrated on FY26). This is equivalent to paying rent only if the lease discount rate equals the WACC; the incremental borrowing rate is not disclosed.
limitations.fix: The weighted incremental borrowing rate from the lease note, and a check of the result against a pre-Ind AS 116 (rent-as-opex) DCF.

limitations.issue: The terminal value is 58% of enterprise value. Return on new capital in perpetuity is set at 20%, equal to Trent's own FY25-FY26 ROIC (19.8%), an analyst decision rather than evidence about returns on stores not yet opened. Because 20% is well above the 13.4% WACC, terminal growth adds value but moves it little (INR 743 to 810 across 5% to 7%).
limitations.fix: Incremental returns on the FY26-FY27 store cohorts once they have two years of trading.

limitations.issue: Beta is set at 1.2 from published market betas (1.28-1.82 for Trent; 0.48-0.52 DMart, 0.94-0.95 V-Mart). No regression on a price series was run because the Screener exports carry no price history.
limitations.fix: A two-to-five-year weekly regression against the NIFTY 50 for Trent and the peers.

limitations.issue: The Star JV, the 20% Zara and Massimo Dutti associates and the MAS JV are added at book value (INR 737 Cr of non-current investments). Star is loss-making; the Inditex stakes are described by management as financial investments.
limitations.fix: A market-value estimate for the Inditex stakes from the associates' earnings and a Star valuation on peer grocery multiples.

limitations.issue: Trent publishes no earnings-call transcripts. Commentary is taken from quarterly press releases, the investor presentation, the Q2 business update and the annual report.
limitations.fix: None available; AGM transcripts if published.

limitations.issue: The FY25 apparel market size (CareEdge) and the Tier II+ share of spend (Wazir, via a secondary source) are the latest published and are older than the macro pack's freshness window; they are flagged as stale overrides.
limitations.fix: A newer CareEdge, Technopak or Wazir release.

limitations.issue: Eight citations are external (market prices, betas, press coverage of the IMF release); one web citation carries no URL. They are graded EXTERNAL, not verified against a held document.
limitations.fix: Archive the external pages as inputs and cite them by hash.
